newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH MONEY MARKET RATES FLAT IN THIN MARKET.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH MONEY MARKET RATES FLAT IN THIN MARKET.

text.p: Dutch money market rates hardly moved Wednesday in a very thin market, becalmed for want of outside influences, dealers said.
"The call (market) was extremely thin. The market is waiting for impulses to start moving again," one trader said.
He expected the call to remain at its actual level as long as there are no new impulses to bring it down.
He added that, theoretically, it was possible for call money to come down a little. "But because the allocation of Dutch Treasury Certificates (DTCs) was tight, rates kept their high level".
Call money moved down a little during the day but rose again to yesterday's level of around 2.75 percent bid.
Yesterday, call money was under considerable upward pressure as DTC settlements created an enduring shortage of liquidity. The central bank announced a new 17-day cash reserve Tuesday afternoon.
This cash reserve is used to cream off excess money market liquidity. It forces commercial banks to draw on their liquid funds to meet the cash reserve requirement.
Trade in one-, two- and three months deposits was limited.
These market rates also kept to Tuesdays' levels, with a slight two basis points rise in 1 year deposits to 3.18 bid. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
